paragraphs: This is This Week in Congress, from Power to the People, for the week ending Saturday, November 21st, 2026.
This briefing is read by a computer voice. Every fact in it comes from public records at Congress.gov, the House Clerk and Senate.gov.
The Senate held 17 recorded votes this week.
On Monday, the Senate confirmed Daniel Desmond Domenico to be U.S. Circuit Judge for the Tenth Circuit, 51 to 46.
On Tuesday, the Senate confirmed Anna St. John to be U.S. Circuit Judge for the Fifth Circuit, 52 to 46.
On Wednesday, the Senate voted to end debate on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, 65 to 31.
On Thursday, the Senate rejected the other chamber's changes to House concurrent resolution 93, 48 to 51.
Also on Thursday, the Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, 62 to 33.
Also on Thursday, the Senate voted to end debate on the nomination of Richard Wesley Bennett, 48 to 46.
On Friday, the Senate confirmed Richard Wesley Bennet to be U.S. District Judge for the Southern District of Texas, 49 to 43.
Also on Friday, the Senate confirmed Courtney Leigh Coker to be U.S. District Judge for the Northern District of Texas, 49 to 41.
The Senate also held nine other votes. Every vote is listed in the app.
The House held four recorded votes this week.
On Tuesday, the House passed two bills under a fast-track rule that needs two thirds: House bill 8483, 398 to 0; and the Common Sense 250 Act of 2026, 365 to 36.
On Wednesday, the House passed the Earth MRI Reauthorization Act of 2026 under a fast-track rule that needs two thirds, 396 to 14.
On Thursday, the House passed the Preventive Health Savings Act under a fast-track rule that needs two thirds, 401 to 0.
The Senate also passed 11 measures without a recorded vote.
The House also passed eight measures without a recorded vote.
No bills became law this week.

Coming up, the Senate next meets Tuesday, November 24th, 2026. The plan: convene for a pro forma session at 3:00 p.m. The House has 16 bills on its schedule for the week of Monday, November 16th, 2026.
That's this week in Congress. You can read every bill and every vote in the app. Thanks for listening.
